minutes.headline: Water commissioners allowed C909 plastic pipe on two projects and backed applying for a PFAS planning grant.
minutes.summary: The board allowed plastic C909 water main for the Round Road and Shirley Road projects, with the superintendent reviewing plans, and plastic service lines with tracer wire. It heard a long debate on a commissioner's PFAS blending proposal versus building a treatment plant, and backed applying for the emerging contaminants grant. It also reviewed a customer collections complaint, a water-purchase option from neighboring towns, and set November meeting dates.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to waive the school's finance charges provided the bills are paid.

what_happened.line: The Water District board allowed plastic C909 water main for the Round Road and Shirley Road projects, with the superintendent reviewing plans.
The board allowed plastic service lines on the Round Road project if tracer wire is installed.
The board approved the engineer applying for the emerging contaminants grant, going for the larger figure that includes Hickory Hills.
A long discussion compared a commissioner's PFAS blending proposal with building a treatment plant; no resolution was reached.
The board moved its November meetings to the 4th and 18th, and agreed to waive the school's finance charges if the bills are paid.

why_it_matters: The pipe material and the PFAS path (blending or a treatment plant) shape what water customers will be asked to pay for, and the treatment decision is still open.
The grant covers planning and design only, so it does not by itself fund a plant; construction would still need a funding vote.
